SD: Consent must be voluntary, informed, and explicitly given for personal information (PI) processing.
When the purpose, method, or type of personal information being processed changes, it is necessary to re-obtain consent.

Personal data should be processed only to the extent necessary. Controllers shall not require non-essential permissions, nor deny access to core functionalities or repeatedly prompt users solely because they refuse such permissions.
The name or surname and contact details of the personal information processor shall be provided truthfully, accurately and completely.
The methods for individuals to access, copy, transfer, delete, correct, supplement, or restrict the processing of their personal information must be clearly defined.

Before processing personal information, the personal information processor shall, in a conspicuous manner and in clear and comprehensible language, truthfully, accurately, and completely inform the individual of the rules governing the processing of personal information.
When personal information processing rules change, the processor shall promptly inform individuals of the changes.
The third-party recipient's name, contact information, processing purpose, method, and data types shall be informed to the individual, except as prescribed by laws and administrative regulations.

For information pushes or commercial marketing to individuals, either options not based on personal traits shall be provided, or a convenient way to opt out of automated decision-making services shall be offered.
A processor shall obtain an individual's separate consent that is genuine, valid, and freely given before disclosing the personal data it has processed.

Processing sensitive personal information (biometrics, religious beliefs, specific identities, medical health, financial accounts, location data, etc.) requires prior separate consent from the individual.

Minors and their guardians shall be informed of the purpose, method, necessity, data types, and protection measures for processing minors' personal information, except as prescribed by laws/regulations.
Corresponding security technical measures shall be taken to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of personal information.
Individuals shall have the right to withdraw consent.

Personal information shall be deleted; however, if the statutory retention period has not expired or deletion is technically difficult, the processor shall cease all processing except storage and necessary security measures.
Personal information processors shall establish convenient mechanisms for accepting and handling individuals' requests to exercise their rights.
Personal information processors shall promptly respond to individuals' rights requests and timely, fully, accurately inform them of handling opinions or results.
